note: Lags are outflow-peak time differences for the two 2022 Indus waves (earlier crest around 23-25 Aug, later crest around 30 Aug-8 Sep), matched separately at each end of the reach. Daily Annexure-I sampling is 06:00, so each peak time is coarse by about +/-12 h. attenuation_ratio is the median of downstream peak outflow divided by upstream peak outflow; above 1 means tributary gain.

Lags are outflow-peak time differences for the two 2022 Indus waves (earlier crest around 23-25 Aug, later crest around 30 Aug-8 Sep), matched separately at each end of the reach. Daily Annexure-I sampling is 06:00, so each peak time is coarse by about +/-12 h. attenuation_ratio is the median of downstream peak outflow divided by upstream peak outflow; above 1 means tributary gain. Kotri's FFC 06:00 outflow was 584,000 on 5, 6, 7 and 8 Sep, so the crest time is only known to about +/-36 h, wider than the usual +/-12 h. 8 Sep is the last day of that plateau. Dawn's 10 Sep 06:00 figure of 600,018 (https://www.dawn.com/news/1709397) is about 2.7% higher and the article attributes it to Manchhar Lake and an MNVD breach, so it is not used as the routed Indus peak. The earlier wave did not form a separate crest at Kotri; the 06:00 series was still rising.
